transcript:
Header: 2025-03-20 16:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Aurora Head of Partnerships), Sofia Ruiz (Aurora SA), Diego Morales (Aurora BD)

Summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Aurora Compute. Covered GTM fit, integration models (API, dedicated, private), compliance needs, and initial benchmarking/pilot plan. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. How are you all?
00:08 Raj: good, thanks Maya. I'm Raj, head of partnerships at Aurora Compute. We have Sofia and Diego on the line. Appreciate you taking the time.
00:15 Liam: hi folks, yeah quick agenda - intro, what Aurora is looking for, technical constraints, and then next steps. Does that sound good?
00:22 Sofia: yep that's perfect. I'm mostly focused on integration feasibility and security.
00:26 Diego: and I'm looking at commercial fit and co-sell opportunities.
00:30 Maya: great. Raj, can you give a quick overview of Aurora? I read the site but want to hear your GTM angle.
00:36 Raj: sure. Aurora's a cloud and GPU infra provider, we do coloc-like racks plus an interconnect overlay for low-latency GPU clusters. We're seeing demand from enterprises wanting per-tenant isolation for LLM workloads. We're exploring partner plays with inference platforms that can run on our dedicated pools or integrate via API.
00:53 Maya: awesome. That maps well to Redwood's dedicated and private modes - we can run in a hosted fashion, in dedicated reserved pools, or as a private deployment in customer VPCs. Quick qual question: are you targeting the same customers as Redwood or more infra-first partners?
01:10 Raj: mix - some infra-first, some SI partners who want a managed inference layer for customers. We want an inference partner that supports predictable throughput and good instrumentation so our platform ops can SLA a stack.
01:24 Liam: when you say predictable throughput, are you thinking about per-tenant QoS, reserved capacity, or burstable pools?
01:30 Raj: mostly reserved capacity for enterprise accounts, plus occasional burst into shared pools. Also important: ability to pin model versions and to have audit logs for compliance.
01:40 Maya: totally - those are standard asks. On audit logs and compliance, we can surface token-level usage and per-call metadata, and we integrate with KMS for encryption at rest. Would that align?
01:52 Sofia: yes, and SOC 2 and ISO are baseline - do you have customer-facing security docs?
01:58 Maya: we do. I'll share a security pack (SOC2 summary, data flow, SSO/SAML guidance) after this call. Link to partner folder: https://redwood.example/partner-deck (note: placeholder link).
02:10 Diego: great. On the tech side Sofia, any particular constraints we should flag?
02:14 Sofia: latency SLOs for real-time chat features are tight - sub 200ms token latency end-to-end is ideal. Also some customers want private deployments inside VPC or even on-prem racks for data residency.
02:28 Liam: ok that latency target is helpful. Our runtime has continuous batching and smart routing - for sub-200ms you'd likely be looking at shorter context lengths or pinned dedicated capacity with optimized kernels. For very low latency we also recommend specific quantization profiles and possibly model variants.
02:45 Raj: can Redwood run inside our control plane, like a private deployment that you manage or do customers self-manage?
02:52 Maya: we have a private mode where the control plane is customer-managed and we provide the runtime package. There's also a managed private control plane option for strategic partners. We can talk licensing.
03:04 Raj: ok. One more thing - do you support multi-tenant isolation on the runtime side?
03:09 Liam: yes, we support strict tenant isolation and per-tenant quotas/limits, and we can route requests to dedicated pools. There are tradeoffs for cost/unit with isolation, we can model those.
03:22 Diego: speaking of cost, how does Redwood think about batching vs latencies? Our sales leads will push for lower cost but product teams won't accept latency regressions.
03:33 Liam: good question - Redwood Optimize suggests batching/caching settings by workload. For interactive UIs we recommend minimal batching and prefix caching; for high throughput jobs you can increase batch sizes and get better unit economics. We can run workload-specific simulations during a POC.
03:48 Raj: sounds good. What do you usually include in a partner pilot?
03:52 Maya: typically a week of perf tests on representative prompts, a small integration test with our API, and an evaluation of cost/latency tradeoffs. For Aurora specifically we could run tests on a dedicated pool you supply or run against Redwood's hosted endpoints with comparable hardware.
04:08 Sofia: we'd prefer tests on Aurora hardware to validate our infra. Can we get a benchmark template?
04:13 Liam: yes I'll send our benchmark template and a checklist for environment parity.
04:18 Raj: on legal/compliance, we'll need an NDA to share some internal infra diagrams.
04:22 Maya: we have a standard partner NDA - I'll share it.

10:12 Maya: (later) quick question - do you have customers in regulated verticals already?
10:16 Raj: a few pilot customers in healthcare and finance, so compliance is a real ask.
10:22 Sofia: we'll need KMS/HSM integration details and audit log retention policies.
10:28 Maya: noted. We'll include KMS integration doc and retention options in the security pack.

18:05 Liam: technical note: when you run on GPUs with different memory profiles, we may recommend model quantization to fit larger context windows - there can be small delta in output quality; we normally run evals to quantify that.
18:20 Sofia: that's acceptable if you show the evals; product teams want to see sample outputs and regression numbers.
18:26 Liam: understood. We'll include sample evals in the POC.

25:40 Diego: what's the go-to-market motion? Co-sell? Referral? Joint marketing?
25:46 Raj: Aurora prefers a partner tier model with co-sell leads for strategic accounts.
25:50 Maya: Redwood does co-sell and a referral program; for strategic partners we do joint playbooks and enablement. We can put together a draft GTM motion next week.

33:12 Maya: circling back to next steps - propose we: 1) exchange NDAs/security contacts, 2) Redwood sends partner one-pager and pricing matrix, 3) schedule a tech deep dive for benchmarks, and 4) both align on pilot scope (hardware, models, eval prompts).
33:34 Raj: agreed.
33:36 Sofia: agreed.

42:00 Maya: ok final recap of action items - Maya will send partner deck and NDA; Liam will share bench template and propose times for deep dive; Raj to confirm Aurora infra contacts and stakeholders. We'll aim to reconvene after the NDA and initial materials are shared.
42:20 Diego: perfect. Thanks everyone.
42:25 Maya: thanks all - I'll follow up with calendar invites and links.

End transcript.

References/links mentioned: https://redwood.example/partner-deck, benchmark-template (drive link to be shared), security pack (SOC2 summary)

Recap/Next Steps: - Redwood to share partner one-pager, pricing, security pack, and NDA by 2025-03-22. - SE to share benchmark template and propose tech deep dive slots by 2025-03-27. - Aurora to confirm stakeholders and infra contacts by 2025-03-25.
